overview: Portreath is a small fishing village and harbour on the north coast, about three miles from Redruth, built around a stream valley that runs down to the beach. West of the harbour breakwater, the sandy beach is popular with families and surfers, with lifeguards in summer and a car park, café and toilets close by.
It was once a busy mining port, and the village still has plenty of character, as well as easy access to the coast path along the clifftops.

expect.title: The beach
expect.text: A sandy beach beside the harbour wall, popular with surfers.

expect.title: The harbour
expect.text: A historic harbour that once served the mines inland.

expect.title: Amy’s Cove
expect.text: A smaller cove right next to the main beach.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: About three miles west-north-west of Redruth.

week.text: An easy family beach with a village feel. Combine it with a clifftop walk or a look at the mining heritage sites inland around Camborne and Redruth.

pairWith.why: another surf beach up the coast
a jewellery workshop and visitor attraction nearby

tips: It faces north, so on windy days the south coast can be calmer.
